To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) Alm and its analogs, (2) the S4L4S voltage sensors, and (3) a mixture of the S4L44 voltage sensors are all able to form pores and kill spiroplasma cells.

(i) the anti-bacterial activities and the pore-formation properties of the two peptide families are correlated, and (ii) the critical residue for the highest efficiency of Alm was found to be proline-14.

(i) voltage-dependent pore-forming peptides can inhibit the growth of bacteria, (ii) their anti-bacterial activity is correlated with their pore-formation ability, (iii) the anti-bacterial mechanism of these peptides is predominantly pore-formation, (iv) the pore-forming ability of these peptides is dependent on the number of monomers forming the pores, (v) the anti-bactericidal mechanism of voltage-dependent pore formers is not related to the 'raft-like' mechanism
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new anti-bacterial peptides with high efficiency, selectivity and low toxicity.
the relationship between the pore-forming properties of two families of voltage-dependent peptides and their anti-bacterial activities.
the development of new antimicrobial peptides with a high efficiency against Gram-positive and Gram-negative bacteria and mycoplasmas.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
anti-bacterial activities correlate with the mean number of monomer per conducting aggregate and the mean open time.
the higher the anti-bacterial efficiency, the higher the mean number of monomeric subunits per pore and the longer the pore open times.
pore-formation, as well as pore size and stability, is the main determinant of the anti-bacterial activities.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the anti-bacterial activities are correlated with the pore-forming properties of the peptides, and are not related to their ability to induce cell agglutinations, to promote cell deformation or depolarization of the target cell plasma membrane.
pore-forming activity is the major determinant for the anti-biological activity of these two classes of channel-forming peptides.
the anti-bacterial activities are related to the pore-forming abilities of Alm and S4L peptides, but that the pore size is the most relevant parameter.
The main takeaway from our work is that
pore-forming activity is the major mechanism of action of these voltage-gated peptides against bacteria.
the pore size is a major determinant for anti-bacterial activity.

the anti-bacterial activities observed with voltage-dependent channel-formers are not due to a simple interaction between a single peptide and the plasma membrane, but to the formation of a pore through which the cell loses its turgor pressure.
